form_title: Exposure to Violent Content on YouTube and Aggressive Behavior Among Teenagers in India: A Correlational Study
form_description: This questionnaire is part of a Mid Semester Review dissertation study conducted at the School of Communications, XIM University. Your participation is completely voluntary, and all responses will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for academic research purposes.

sections.section_title: Section 1: Informed Consent and Participant Information

questions.question_text: Do you consent to voluntarily participate in this study?

options: 20 years or older (Note: Responses from participants aged 20 and above will be filtered out during data cleaning as the study focuses specifically on teenagers aged 13–19)

questions.question_text: Do you use YouTube on a regular basis (at least a few times a week)?

sections.section_title: Section 2: YouTube Usage Patterns & Exposure to Violent Content

questions.question_text: On average, how much time do you spend watching YouTube daily?
Which features on YouTube do you use or encounter the most? (Check all that apply)
How often do you encounter violent content (such as physical fights, weapons, aggressive crime scenes, or intense brawls) on YouTube?
When you encounter violent content on YouTube, how does it usually happen?
options: It appears through the recommendation algorithm
It shows up on YouTube Shorts
It is autoplayed after another video

questions.question_text: When you see violent videos on YouTube, how realistic do you feel they are compared to real-life violence?

sections.instructions: Rate each statement on a 5-point scale from 1 (Extremely uncharacteristic of me) to 5 (Extremely characteristic of me).

questions.statement: Given enough provocation, I may hit another person.
There are people who pushed me so far that we came to blows.
If somebody hits me, I hit back.
I can't help getting into arguments when people disagree with me.
My friends say that I argue a lot.
I tell my friends openly when I disagree with them angrily.
I flare up quickly but get over it fast.
Sometimes I feel like a powder keg ready to explode.
When I am frustrated, I display my temper outwardly.
I sometimes feel that people are laughing at me behind my back.
When people are nice, I wonder what they want.
I wonder what hidden reasons lie behind the good things people do for me.

questions.question_text: How often do your friends share or discuss violent or action-heavy videos with you?
Do your parents or guardians monitor, discuss, or set limits on what you watch on YouTube?
How often do you watch YouTube content unsupervised in a private space (e.g., your own room late at night)?
